steps.what: Read the funding call and identify proposal requirements
Choose the research question, mathematical approach and collaboration commitments
Prepare the research budget and justify requested resources
Write grant proposals from the research design and checked budget

loop.purpose: Draft funder-specific prose around the lecturer's actual research design
loop.input: checked call requirements, research design, verified references and budget
loop.output: sectioned proposal draft with source references
loop.check: Lecturer checks mathematical claims, novelty, feasibility, references and consistency with the budget; unsupported commitments are removed
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence or unclear novelty is written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A form can enforce headings but cannot express the rationale of a new mathematical research project

steps.what: Check the final proposal's science, commitments and call compliance
Submit the final proposal package to the funding body

tasks.design: Start with the funder's native application template in {DOCS} and an existing costing workbook in {SPREADSHEET}. A bounded prose draft uses the lecturer's research design and verified references; the lecturer checks the complete package before a separate submission through the {OTHER} funding application portal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each call requires a new explanation of the research and a differently structured application.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates handle section structure and costing; bounded drafting can adapt supplied scientific material without inventing the research.
tasks.still_hard: Original mathematics, credible feasibility and genuine collaborator commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a worthwhile research question and defending its scientific contribution.
tasks.altitude: Less application assembly while retaining scientific authorship and responsibility.

reach.task: Check a proposal's completeness against the funding call
reach.learn: Eligibility rules and institutional costing practice

evidence.claim: Call templates, checked costing formulas and bounded proposal drafting are model knowledge designs; the digest does not establish grant-writing time savings.

assumptions: Boundary is the lecturer's real application work through submission, including proposal writing and budget preparation. Collaborator research and any existing institutional sign-off are other-role work and receive no saving; no new approval process is invented.

The lecturer produces section requirements and deadline from the call in s1, research aims and methods in s2, and staff months, cost categories, rates and totals in s3. Finance supplies approved rates through its existing work. Capture and verification are retained in those steps; unknown rates or eligibility are resolved manually, not estimated by a model.

Verified references are supplied and checked within s2's research design work; no generated citation is treated as a source. The final portal attachment names, call ID and package version are confirmed in s6, whose full existing time is retained.
Test native call templates and existing costing workbooks before custom code. An author's ordinary save has no separate gate or saving; the gate here covers the external submission.
unknowns: Which calls and budget templates recur
Whether the lecturer or a research office performs the actual submission
research_questions: Does drafting reduce total writing and correction time without weakening mathematical accuracy or adding unsupported commitments?

already_counted.description: Capture call requirements, verify costing and correct the scientific draft and final package

incremental.description: Maintain call-specific templates and sample unsupported draft claims

approvals.approved_version: The exact final call ID, narrative, reference list, budget and attachment versions checked in s5; any change invalidates submission approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=80.75, gross=19.25, upkeep=2, net=17.25. Cautious case: a one-off call retains all 15 requirement hours and all 15 budget hours, while difficult mathematical prose retains 30 of 35 writing hours; all other 35 hours stay, giving 5 gross minus 2 upkeep =3. High 11 retains more scientific rewriting than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in campus and community events

steps.what: Review the campus or community event programme and intended audience
Prepare the mathematical demonstration or contribution used at the event
Participate in campus and community events and answer audience questions

tasks.design: Use the existing {DOCS} event brief and a reusable set of checked mathematical demonstrations. The lecturer adapts the actual contribution and participates in person; no attendance log, follow-up report or automated message is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful demonstrations can be scattered across old teaching and outreach material.
tasks.enabler_now: An organised native document collection can make checked material easier to find and adapt.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the audience, answering spontaneous questions and representing the institution.
tasks.human_edge: Making mathematics accessible through responsive personal interaction.

ambition.what: Offer an existing demonstration in a more accessible format for attendees unfamiliar with university mathematics.

tasks.altitude: A little less preparation for events that reuse a demonstration; the public-facing role stays unchanged.

reach.task: Match a demonstration to an event audience
reach.learn: Audience accessibility and outreach format constraints

evidence.claim: Reuse of checked event demonstrations and a native event-brief view are model knowledge estimates, with no digest evidence of measured participation savings.

assumptions: Boundary includes reviewing the event brief, preparing a real contribution and attending. Event organisation and travel are not claimed as savings. No record is invented for participation; s2 is the material actually used with the audience.

The organiser supplies audience, time, venue, participation format and accessibility needs in the existing brief. s1 counts reading and clarification; missing information is clarified manually. The lecturer selects and checks demonstration content in s2, including any figures or exercise answers.

Native document folders, search and existing demonstration templates are tested first. s1 saves only repeated document navigation; s2 saves reused layout and standard example assembly, not mathematical verification. Same-system saves have no added gate or benefit.
unknowns: How often participation involves a prepared demonstration rather than attendance only
Whether suitable checked material already exists
research_questions: Which recurring events reuse a contribution, and how much actual preparation disappears?

already_counted.description: Read event details and adapt and check the actual contribution

incremental.description: Retire outdated demonstrations and maintain the small reusable collection

approvals.approved_version: The audience-specific contribution version and the lecturer's live answers; new audience questions require fresh human judgement

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=94, gross=6, upkeep=0.5, net=5.5. Cautious case: an event needs a new contribution or only attendance, so reuse is not deployed, all current work remains and there is no collection upkeep for that case: zero. High 3 retains additional adaptation for unfamiliar audience needs; no attendance time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define the assignment's mathematical topic, level and reading purpose
Search library catalogues for specialized materials matching the reading criteria
Read candidate materials and select appropriate mathematical readings
Capture and verify citation metadata and accessible reading locations
Compile bibliographies from the verified citation records
Check and publish the final reading bibliography for students

tasks.design: Use native saved library searches and a citation manager in {OTHER}, then format the verified selections into {DOCS}. The lecturer reads and chooses the materials, checks bibliographic identity and student access, and separately publishes the final bibliography in {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated catalogue navigation and manual citation formatting surround the substantive reading selection.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved searches and deterministic citation formatting already handle those mechanical operations.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing prerequisites, mathematical correctness and the suitability of specialized readings.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a reading that stretches students without exceeding their mathematical preparation.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting, with the same responsibility for reading selection and access.

reach.task: Check whether assigned readings are accessible to the intended students
reach.learn: Library holdings, stable identifiers and licensing constraints

evidence.claim: Saved library searches and deterministic citation-manager formatting are model knowledge capabilities; no local measured saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary includes criteria, literature search, substantive selection, citation capture, formatting and actual student publication. Existing course design is an input rather than a saving. No model-generated title or reference is accepted as bibliographic evidence.

The {OTHER} categories are the library catalogue and citation manager. The lecturer produces author, title, year, edition, identifier, chapter or page range and verified student-access link in s4 by importing and checking publisher or catalogue records. All 10 capture hours remain; incomplete metadata is keyed and verified manually before s5 runs.

The required style and selected record IDs are confirmed in s5's input contract from the course requirements and s4. If citation fields cannot support the style, formatting returns to manual work. s6 retains checking the exact formatted output and link destinations before publication.

Test native saved searches and citation-manager export before custom code. Formatting is draft production, while the actual publication is a separate gated action; ordinary author saves have no gate or saving.
unknowns: Coverage and quality of citation metadata in the relevant mathematical sources
Current use of citation-manager export and library saved searches
research_questions: Do imported edition and chapter metadata survive export without increasing correction time?

already_counted.description: Verify bibliographic records and check the final bibliography before publication

incremental.description: Maintain saved searches and citation-style configuration

approvals.approved_version: Exact formatted bibliography version, selected editions and access links checked at publication; any change requires a fresh final check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=85.5, gross=14.5, upkeep=1, net=13.5. Cautious case: specialist searches save nothing and incomplete edition metadata require manual correction, retaining 7 of 10 formatting hours; all other 90 hours remain, so 3 gross minus 1 upkeep =2. High 9 assumes better metadata coverage while retaining more formatting correction than central.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The lecturer keeps research originality, reading selection and public participation while reducing selected assembly work.
reach: Check funder requirements with research administration and reading access with library colleagues
role.ambitious_version: Use existing demonstrations to make mathematical ideas accessible to new audiences without reducing scholarly standards.
